description: Server Components are the default component type in the Next.js App Router. They render exclusively on the server, produce a React Server Component Payload (RSC Payload), and never ship JavaScript to the client bundle. They enable direct data access close to the source, protect secrets, reduce client-side JavaScript, improve First Contentful Paint (FCP), and allow progressive streaming. They are composable with Client Components through prop-passing and the children/slot pattern, maintaining a strict server/client boundary.

constraints.title: No Browser APIs in Server Components
constraints.problem: Browser-only globals such as window, document, localStorage, sessionStorage, navigator, and location cannot be accessed inside Server Components.
constraints.whyItMatters: Server Components execute only in the Node.js server runtime. There is no browser context, no DOM, and no Web APIs. Any usage will throw a ReferenceError at runtime or during build, crashing the render and returning a 500 error to users.
allowedPatterns: async/await data fetching
Node.js built-ins (fs, path, crypto)
Server-side environment variables (process.env.SECRET)
Database queries (ORM, raw SQL)
cookies() from next/headers
headers() from next/headers
productionRisks: ReferenceError crashing the server render
500 errors served to users
Build failures in strict mode
Broken pages when deployed to serverless environments
architectureImplications: Browser interaction logic must live in Client Components
Server Components define the static structure and data-fetching layer
Interactivity is an explicit opt-in via 'use client'
optimizationGuidance: Keep Server Components purely data-driven and stateless
Push all browser-API usage to the smallest possible Client Component leaf nodes
quickFixes: Add 'use client' at the top of the file if the component needs browser APIs
Extract only the browser-dependent part into a separate Client Component and import it
architectureSuggestions: Design components so that the Server Component fetches and owns data, and a thin Client Component handles display/interaction
Use the children/slot pattern to pass server-rendered subtrees into client wrappers

invalid:
export default async function Page() { const stored = localStorage.getItem('token'); return
{stored}
}
valid:
export default async function Page() { const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data'); const json = await data.json(); return
{json.title}
}

constraints.title: No React Hooks in Server Components
constraints.problem: React hooks (useState, useEffect, useReducer, useContext, useRef, useCallback, useMemo, useTransition, useDeferredValue, useId, useLayoutEffect, useInsertionEffect) cannot be used in Server Components.
constraints.whyItMatters: Hooks are part of the React client runtime and rely on the fiber reconciler running in the browser. Server Components are rendered to the RSC Payload in a one-shot server pass with no reconciler, no state tree, and no effect scheduling. Attempting to use hooks causes an immediate runtime error.
allowedPatterns: async/await instead of useEffect for data loading
Direct variable declarations instead of useState for static values
Server-side caching (use cache directive, unstable_cache) instead of useMemo
React.cache() for request-scoped memoization
productionRisks: Build-time errors that block deployment
Runtime crashes breaking entire route segments
Invalid RSC Payload causing client reconciliation failures
architectureImplications: All stateful and reactive logic must be isolated in Client Components
Server Components are pure render functions that accept props and return JSX
optimizationGuidance: Replace useEffect data-loading with top-level async/await in Server Components
Use React.cache() for deduplicating expensive server-side computations within a request
quickFixes: Add 'use client' to any file using hooks
Move hook-dependent logic to a dedicated Client Component file
architectureSuggestions: Establish a clear rule: Server Components are async functions that return JSX; Client Components are interactive leaf nodes
Wrap context providers in dedicated 'use client' files imported by the root layout

invalid:
'use server'
export default function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); return <button onClick={() => setCount(c => c+1)}>{count}</button> }

constraints.title: No Event Handlers in Server Components
constraints.problem: Event handler props (onClick, onChange, onSubmit, onKeyDown, onMouseOver, etc.) cannot be attached inside Server Components.
constraints.whyItMatters: Event handlers are JavaScript callbacks that run in the browser. Server Components produce static RSC Payload with no JavaScript bundle output. Attaching event handlers in a Server Component means those handlers will never execute because no JavaScript is shipped for them.
allowedPatterns: Server Actions bound to <form action={...}> for declarative mutation handling
Passing event handlers as serialized props from Server to Client Components
productionRisks: Silent failures: button clicks and form submissions do nothing
Confusing UX with non-interactive-looking interactive elements
Security risk if a developer mistakenly assumes a handler executed server-side
architectureImplications: Interactive UI must be architected as Client Components
Forms in Server Components should use Server Actions (action prop) for mutation
optimizationGuidance: Use Server Actions with <form action={serverAction}> for mutation patterns to keep the component server-rendered
Create isolated Client Component wrappers only for the interactive element, not the whole page
quickFixes: Extract the interactive element into a 'use client' component
For form submissions, replace onClick handlers with a Server Action passed to <form action={}>
architectureSuggestions: Design page-level components as Server Components with Server Actions for mutations, and extract interactive controls as small Client Component islands

invalid: export default function Page() { return <button onClick={() => console.log('clicked')}>Click</button> }
valid:
'use client'
export default function Button() { return <button onClick={() => console.log('clicked')}>Click</button> }

constraints.title: Environment Variable Exposure via Server Components
constraints.problem: Non-public environment variables accessed in Server Components can be accidentally leaked to the client if the file is also imported into a Client Component module graph.
constraints.whyItMatters: Next.js only includes environment variables prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_ in the client bundle. However, if a utility module containing server-only logic (API keys, secrets, database credentials) is imported into a Client Component, those variables are replaced with empty strings, breaking functionality silently rather than throwing an error. In some misuse patterns, secrets could be serialized into RSC props and exposed.
forbiddenPatterns: Importing server-side utility files (with API keys, DB credentials) into Client Components
Passing raw secret values as props from Server to Client Components
Using process.env.SECRET_KEY inside components without server-only guard
Exporting functions that contain secrets from shared module files
allowedPatterns: import 'server-only' at the top of any file with server-exclusive logic
Passing sanitized DTOs (Data Transfer Objects) as props — never raw database records
Prefixing truly public variables with NEXT_PUBLIC_
Using the taint API (experimental) to prevent sensitive objects from crossing to client
productionRisks: API key exposure in client bundles
Database credential leakage
Silent broken behavior when secrets become empty strings on the client
Security audit failures
architectureImplications: A clear Data Access Layer (DAL) enforces server-only data access patterns
Server Components should return sanitized, minimal DTOs rather than full database records
optimizationGuidance: Create a dedicated lib/dal.ts (Data Access Layer) marked with import 'server-only'
Never pass raw database rows as props; serialize minimal, safe fields
quickFixes: Add import 'server-only' to any file containing secrets or database access
Audit all props passed from Server to Client Components for sensitive data
architectureSuggestions: Establish a Data Access Layer (DAL) as the sole entry point for data, marked server-only, performing authorization checks and returning minimal DTOs

invalid:
// lib/data.ts (no server-only guard)
export async function getUser() { return fetch(url, { headers: { authorization: process.env.API_SECRET } }) }

constraints.title: React Context Not Supported in Server Components
constraints.problem: createContext and useContext cannot be used directly in Server Components.
constraints.whyItMatters: React context is a client-side state propagation mechanism that requires the reconciler. Server Components have no context tree. Attempting to consume context in a Server Component will result in a runtime error or undefined values.
forbiddenPatterns: Wrapping the root layout's body with a context provider that is itself a Server Component
allowedPatterns: Creating a 'use client' context provider component that wraps children
Importing the client provider into the root layout (server component) and passing children through
Passing data via props from Server to Client Components instead of context when possible
productionRisks: Runtime crashes when context is accessed in server-rendered subtrees
Overly broad 'use client' boundaries inflating bundle size when wrapping too high in the tree
architectureImplications: Context providers are always Client Components
Providers should wrap as deep in the tree as possible to minimize the Client Component surface area
Global state that depends on server data should be fetched server-side and passed as props to the provider
optimizationGuidance: Render context providers as deep as possible in the component tree to keep the static server-rendered outer shell large
Prefer prop drilling or URL state for simple cases to avoid adding a context provider at all
quickFixes: Create a new file with 'use client' for the context and provider
Import that provider into the Server Component layout and wrap children with it
architectureSuggestions: Use a pattern where the Server Component fetches data, then passes it as initial props to a 'use client' provider, minimizing client-side fetching

constraints.title: Mutations Must Not Occur During Server Component Rendering
constraints.problem: Side effects like setting cookies, invalidating caches, or writing to a database must not happen during the render phase of a Server Component.
constraints.whyItMatters: Next.js explicitly prevents setting cookies or triggering cache revalidation within render methods to prevent unintended side effects. Mutations during render break the predictability of prerendering and caching, and can cause stale data, double-writes, and security vulnerabilities.
forbiddenPatterns: cookies().set() or cookies().delete() inside a Server Component render
revalidateTag() inside a Server Component render
revalidatePath() inside a Server Component render
Database writes inside a Server Component render function
Triggering mutations based on searchParams during render
allowedPatterns: Server Actions for all data mutations
<form action={serverAction}> for form-based mutations
revalidateTag() and revalidatePath() called from Server Actions or Route Handlers only
productionRisks: Double-execution of mutations during development (Strict Mode double-render)
Cache poisoning from mutations during prerendering
Stale data served after a mutation that was silently suppressed
Security vulnerabilities from unauthorized mutations on page load
architectureImplications: Read operations belong in Server Component render; write operations belong in Server Actions
Route Handlers are the correct boundary for webhook-style mutation triggers
optimizationGuidance: Centralize all mutations in Server Actions co-located with the UI that triggers them
Always pair a mutation Server Action with revalidateTag to keep cache coherent
quickFixes: Move the mutation logic into an async function marked 'use server'
Attach that Server Action to a <form> or call it from a Client Component event handler
architectureSuggestions: Use the pattern: Server Component renders read data → Client Component handles interaction → Server Action handles mutation and revalidation

invalid: export default async function Page({ searchParams }) { if (searchParams.logout) { (await cookies()).delete('session') } return <Profile /> }
